as_told.title: Documentary clip: binary model explains celestial observations

plain: The idea is that our Sun has an unseen partner star, and the two of them circling each other drives the Great Year, a very long cycle in the sky that ancient peoples counted. It comes from a documentary called The Great Year, which Michels plays on an episode about events around 12,000 BC. The researcher Matt LaCroix sums up the film's argument. He says its makers "postulated that the great year was based on a dance of our binary companion," and that some of them "thought it was Sirius," the bright star. In a clip from the film, the narrator adds that "some say the binary model confirms all of our Celestial observations without the need for excessive torque or epicycle type explanations." Neither teller names a source beyond the film. If it were true, a slow shift in the sky usually blamed on Earth's wobble would instead be a sign of a second sun.
